Quotes / Blaise Pascal / Q0392

English

All of humanity’s misfortune comes from one thing: not knowing how to remain quietly in a room.
Thinker Blaise Pascal
School Proto-Existential Christian Thought
Source Pensées (common numbering)
Theme Philosophy

Context and commentary are editorial aids for reading. They do not replace the primary text or scholarly commentary.

Source context

This English passage is associated with Pensées (common numbering), within the tradition of Proto-Existential Christian Thought. The wording below is a verified rendering prepared for careful reading rather than a claim of unique translation authority.

A short reading

Read in the register of philosophy, the sentence asks the reader to test an assumption rather than to collect a slogan. In Blaise Pascal's wider work, similar claims are usually offered as prompts for judgment: what would have to be true for the sentence to hold, and what would follow if it did?
